newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends down on speculative selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends down on speculative selling.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Wednesday on speculative selling from retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,140 yuan ($378) per tonne, losing 14 yuan. It opened at 3,150 and hit a high of 3,160 yuan per tonne.
November fell two to 3,160 yuan, the January 1998 contract 17 to 3,131, March rose 96 to 3,151 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 20,400 tonnes from 27,900 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly lower and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Speculative selling is responsible for today's falls with many investors putting more faith in the chance of further falls in the long run than of rises," one trader said.
"There are also many investors liquidating their long positions and injecting money into other active markets," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to fall steadily in the next few days if no special market-moving news came to light.
